To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the most suitable simulation model for WSN is the physical model, since it is more accurate, but it is also more complex, thus it is not always scalable; 2) the most suitable tool for WSN simulation depends on the application and the model to be implemented.

1) the simulation of WSN requires a suitable model and a suitable framework, 2) there is not a single framework that is suitable for all purposes, 3) the accuracy and the scalability are two conflicting requirements and 4) there are no tools that are suitable for all purposes.

(i) the simulation model should be based on a suitable abstraction of WSN and (ii) the simulation framework should be able to handle the simulation of large networks, and it should provide an accurate enough physical layer model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
simulation tools that are suitable to model wireless networks.
the design and development of a simulation framework for WSN.
the simulation tools for WSN, with a focus on the modeling of the physical layer.

there is no single simulator for WSN, but there are several simulators, each one with its own advantages and drawbacks, which can be used depending on the particular scenario, the hardware, the physical layer, etc.
the best tool for WSN simulation depends on the application under study and the available computational resources.
there is not a unique solution for simulating WSN, but the most appropriate one depends on the application, the scenario, and the available resources.
